sekcje: Drug Levels and Effects > Summary of Use during Lactation

The amount of pibrentasvir in breastmilk was very low in a small preliminary study, consistent with its high protein binding of >99.9%. If a mother requires pibrentasvir or the combination of glecaprevir and pibrentasvir, it is not a reason to discontinue breastfeeding.
Hepatitis C is not transmitted through breastmilk, and breastmilk has been shown to inactivate hepatitis C virus (HCV). However, the Centers for Disease Control recommends that mothers with HCV infection should consider abstaining from breastfeeding if their nipples are cracked or bleeding. It is not clear if this warning would apply to mothers who are being treated for hepatitis C.
Infants born to mothers with HCV infection should be tested for HCV infection; because maternal antibody is present for the first 18 months of life and before the infant mounts an immunologic response, nucleic acid testing is recommended.
Drug Levels and Effects > Drug Levels

Maternal Levels. Four women were taking glecaprevir 300 mg plus pibrentasvir 120 mg orally once daily for chronic hepatitis C infection. Single breastmilk samples were obtained postpartum after at least 2 daily doses, 2 days postpartum (range 1 to 3 days), and 2 to 13 days after starting the combination at a median of 4.5 hours (range 2.1 to 7.4 hours) after the last reported maternal drug intake. The average milk concentration of pibrentasvir was 7.04 mcg/L and the average daily infant dosage was 0.0011 mg/kg. The authors estimated an RID of 0.064% (range 0.0185% to 0.3649%).
Infant Levels. Relevant published information was not found as of the revision date.
